issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters and example usage (Main.java) calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments, but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and implementations use the volume). This parameter mismatch makes the solution incompatible with the specified API and the template's example usage, causing confusion or compile errors when following the instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API with the problem specification and template usage. Either remove the double parameter from Milkable.messageOnMilk(double) in the solution (change to messageOnMilk()) and update Seal/Goat implementations to return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" with no volume, or update the problem statement and template usage to require and pass a volume parameter consistently. The recommended fix is to change the solution's Milkable and its implementations to the no-argument signature to match the UML and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument method messageOnMilk() returning a String (used as m.messageOnMilk()), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and implementations use the double parameter). This mismatched method signature creates a direct API conflict: students following the problem/template will implement or call a no-arg messageOnMilk(), while the solution and its interface require a double parameter, causing confusion and compilation/runtime mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable API consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) change the solution to define Milkable.messageOnMilk() with no parameters and update Seal/Goat implementations to return the expected string ("[Animal Type] [name] is milked"); or (B) update the problem statement and template to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and document the volume parameter in the specification. Prefer (A) to match the current problem description and template usage.
